name: Claude Code
recommended: Complex multi-file refactors and architectural changes
description: Claude Code is Anthropic's terminal-based coding agent with deep reasoning capabilities, subagent delegation, and a plugin system. It excels at complex multi-file refactoring and architectural changes, featuring the highest SWE-bench score in its class (88.6%). Pricing ranges from $20-200/mo with usage-based billing. No local-only mode available.

name: Hermes Agent
recommended: Automated workflows, scheduled tasks, and multi-model setups
description: Hermes Agent is a full-featured open-source terminal coding agent with built-in cron scheduling, multi-provider routing, subagent delegation, and a console dashboard. It supports background tasks, memory persistence, skills system, and MOA (Mixture of Agents) orchestration. Free with BYO API keys. Designed for automated workflows, scheduled tasks, and complex multi-model setups.

name: Cursor
recommended: Everyday interactive development and quick edits
description: Cursor is an AI-native IDE built as a VS Code fork with deep AI integration. It features the Composer for multi-file editing, background agents for parallel tasks, and fast inline editing. SWE-bench score of 91.2%. Pricing $20-200/mo with usage-based billing. No cron/scheduling. Closed source with VS Code fork lock-in.

name: OpenCode
recommended: Open-source alternative with flexible provider choice
description: OpenCode is a skill-driven terminal coding agent with multi-provider support and a slash-command workflow system. It executes SKILL.md files for repeatable coding tasks. SWE-bench score of 88.0%. Free and open source with BYO API keys. Note: project is archived with no active development. No vision support or subagents.

name: Mimo Code
description: Mimo Code is an OpenCode fork that adds vision support and reasoning model integration while maintaining the skill-driven execution model. Free and open source with BYO API keys. Active development with a smaller community than OpenCode. No subagents or cron scheduling.

name: Kilo Code CLI
recommended: Quick code tasks and lightweight terminal work
description: Kilo Code is a lightweight terminal coding agent designed for quick AI-assisted tasks. It features fast startup, usage stats tracking, auto-update, and a console dashboard. Free with BYO API keys. No background tasks, git integration, or plugin system. Best for quick code tasks and lightweight terminal work.

name: pi.dev
description: pi.dev is a terminal agent focused on long-running knowledge-backed agents with persistent knowledge graphs, scheduled tasks, and background agents. Free with BYO API keys. Features cron scheduling and subagent support. No git integration or plugin system. Small community. Best for knowledge-intensive long-running agent tasks.

name: Oh My Pi
description: Oh My Pi is a hash-anchored terminal coding agent with the largest model catalog, vision support, browser automation, LSP integration, and subagent system. Free with BYO API keys. Daily releases (v16+) mean rapid feature iteration but can break configs. No built-in cron. Less polished TUI than commercial alternatives. Best for model experimentation and multi-model workflows.

name: Gitlawb Zero
recommended: Privacy-focused developers who want full control
description: Gitlawb Zero is a decentralized terminal coding agent designed for developers who want full ownership with no vendor lock-in. Free with BYO API keys. Features customizable keyboard shortcuts, Android Termux support, and atomic binary updates. No vision support or subagents. Smaller community. Best for privacy-focused developers who want full control over their coding agent.

name: OpenAI Codex
recommended: Parallel ticket processing and batch tasks
description: OpenAI Codex is a CLI and cloud-based coding agent with parallel Git worktree execution and cloud sandboxed agents. SWE-bench score of 72.8%. Included in ChatGPT Plus ($20-200/mo). Open source CLI but cloud-dependent for parallel mode. OpenAI models only with usage caps on Plus plan. Best for parallel ticket processing and batch tasks.

name: Goose
recommended: Extensible coding agent with MCP tool integration
description: Goose is an extensible open-source terminal coding agent with MCP (Model Context Protocol) support, written in Rust for performance. 51K+ GitHub stars. Free with BYO API keys and supports any LLM. No vision support, subagent system, or built-in cron. Best for developers wanting an extensible coding agent with MCP tool integration.

name: OpenClaw
recommended: Cross-platform AI assistant for daily tasks
description: OpenClaw is a cross-platform desktop AI assistant with vision support, ACP protocol support, cron scheduling, and background tasks. 382K+ GitHub stars. Free and open source. Desktop application (not terminal-based) requiring local installation. No native subagent system. Best for cross-platform personal AI assistant for daily tasks.

name: Codebuff
description: Codebuff is a free, open-source terminal coding agent that uses BYO API keys. It focuses on fast code generation with a clean terminal interface. Codebuff is designed for developers who want a lightweight, no-frills coding agent without IDE dependencies.

name: AmpCode
bestFor: Unconstrained agentic coding with multi-model routing
cons: Free tier closed to new signups
description: AmpCode is a terminal and IDE coding agent with pay-as-you-go pricing (free tier ~$10/day). It offers unconstrained agentic coding with multi-model routing, automatically selecting the best model for each task. AmpCode supports Claude, GPT-4, and other models. Features team thread sharing and built-in code review. Free tier closed to new signups; no flat subscription option.

name: GitHub Copilot CLI
bestFor: GitHub-native terminal agent with PR/issue integration
recommended: Developers in GitHub ecosystem wanting terminal agent
description: GitHub Copilot CLI is GitHub's terminal coding agent, available with a Copilot subscription ($10-39/mo). It integrates natively with GitHub's ecosystem, including PR creation, issue linking, and repository context. Supports multi-model (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5), has built-in MCP server, and a fleet of parallel subagents. Requires Copilot subscription; GitHub ecosystem dependent with premium request quota limits.

name: Cline CLI
description: Cline CLI is a free, open-source terminal coding agent with autonomous coding and browser automation capabilities. 64K+ GitHub stars. It uses BYO API keys and can interact with the browser, run terminal commands, and create/edit files autonomously. Features MCP integration and multi-provider support. No cron or subagents. Resource-heavy. Best for autonomous coding with browser automation.

name: Kimi CLI
description: Kimi CLI is Moonshot AI's free terminal coding agent with BYO API key support. 9K+ GitHub stars. Offers strong code generation and reasoning capabilities with access to Moonshot's Kimi models. Features skills and MCP support, ACP IDE integration. No vision, cron, or subagents. Open source (Apache-2.0). Best for developers wanting Moonshot AI integration.

name: Groq Code CLI
description: Groq Code CLI is a free, open-source terminal coding agent powered by Groq's ultra-fast LPU inference. 737 GitHub stars. It uses BYO API keys and delivers near-instant code generation, making it ideal for rapid iteration cycles. Supports Claude, Llama, and Mixtral models through Groq's API. Groq models only, smaller community, no vision. MIT license. Best for developers needing fast iteration speed.

name: Grok Build CLI
bestFor: xAI's coding agent with parallel execution
description: Grok Build CLI is xAI's free coding agent available to xAI subscribers. 13K+ GitHub stars. Features parallel execution of coding tasks (8 parallel agents), Society of Mind architecture, vision support, subagents, and fullscreen TUI. xAI models only, no cron, newer with less community data. Apache-2.0 license. Best for xAI ecosystem developers.
